meta.title: dix.tax: your Zurich property when you live abroad
meta.description: You own a flat or a house in the canton of Zurich and live in another country. Get the exact numbers for the Zurich tax return, including the debt split and the figures that only set your rate.
meta.guideTitle: Guide: filling in the Zurich form from abroad

hero.title: Your flat is in Zurich. You are not. The tax return still is.
hero.lead: Own a flat in the canton of Zurich but live somewhere else? You still have to file a Zurich tax return. Answer a few plain questions and get the exact number for every line.

items.title: You have to file
items.body: A flat in Zurich makes you a taxpayer here, even if you have never lived in Switzerland. Empty or rented, it counts. The municipality will send you a form.

items.title: Only the flat is taxed
items.body: Your salary and savings at home are not taxed here. You still write them down, because they set the rate on the flat.

items.title: The canton did the maths
items.body: You guess nothing. Zurich has already set the two numbers the form wants. They are on your assessment letter, and the local tax office will send it again.

items.title: Find the letter
items.body: The Schätzungsanzeige from the canton, or last year's tax bill. Both carry the two numbers you need.

items.title: Answer a few questions
items.body: Who uses the flat, and what you own elsewhere. The second part decides how much of your mortgage counts here.

items.title: Copy the numbers across
items.body: You get the Zurich form, line by line, plus a German note to paste in. Type it into ZHprivateTax or the paper form.

cta.title: Ten minutes now beats an estimated assessment later
cta.body: Have the cantonal assessment and your mortgage statement in front of you. That is all you need.

calc.title: Prepare the declaration
calc.lead: Fill in what you know. Your form updates as you type.

year.label: Tax year
year.hint: The return for a year is filed in spring of the following year. Values are as of 31 December.

fields.municipalityHint: The Zurich municipality the property lies in. It is the one that sends your tax return.
fields.shareHint: 100 if you own it alone or together with your spouse
fields.taxValueHint: The tax value from the cantonal assessment, for the whole property. Not the price you paid and not what an agent would ask for it today.
fields.eigenmietwertHint: From the same assessment notice, for the whole property.
fields.rent: Rent received per year, in CHF
fields.rentHint: Without the utilities the tenant pays on top.
fields.maintenanceHint: The flat deduction needs no receipts. Claim the real costs only if they were higher, and keep the invoices.
fields.maintenanceAmount: Costs paid in the year, in CHF

world.title: You, everywhere else
world.lead: None of this is taxed in Switzerland. Zurich needs it to set your rate, and to work out how much of your debt belongs to the Swiss property.
world.assets: Everything you own worldwide, in CHF
world.assetsHint: Gross, before debts, this property included, on 31 December. An approximate figure is better than none: it decides how much of your interest you may deduct.
world.incomeHint: Over the whole year, this property included.
world.debtHint: Mortgages and other loans, on 31 December.
world.interestHint: Over the whole year, on all of those debts.

result.title: Your numbers
result.quotaHint: Your debts and your interest are deductible in this proportion.
result.quotaMissing: Add what you own worldwide and we can work out how much of your debt Zurich accepts. Until then none of it is deducted.
result.rateHint: Declared but not taxed here. It decides the rate the amounts above are taxed at.
result.notTaxed: Only the property is taxed in Switzerland. Everything else you declare is there to set the rate.
result.remarkTitle: Note for the remarks field, in German
result.remarkHint: Paste this into the remarks (Bemerkungen) of your tax return or add it as a separate sheet.

assumptions: The Steuerwert and the Eigenmietwert are taken as you enter them from the cantonal assessment. Nothing is estimated from a purchase price.
Maintenance and administration are deducted at a flat 20% of the gross, unless you enter what you really paid.
Debts and debt interest are split in proportion to where your assets lie, which is the rule for an owner taxed here on the property alone.
Your income and wealth elsewhere are carried through untouched. They set the rate and are not taxed here.
A share below 100% is applied to the value, the income and the costs alike.
One property, held privately, for a full tax year. A purchase, a sale or an inheritance during the year needs an adviser.

guide.title: Filling in the Zurich form from abroad, step by step
guide.lead: The canton's online tax return is called ZHprivateTax. The paper form has the same fields. Here is where everything goes.

steps.title: Open the Liegenschaftenverzeichnis
steps.body: This is the list of real estate. Since tax year 2024 every property is declared here, and the totals are carried to the main form by the program.

steps.title: Add the property
steps.body: Enter the municipality and the street. As type choose Stockwerkeigentum for a flat or Einfamilienhaus for a house, and enter the area in m².

steps.title: Enter the income
steps.body: In the field Eigenmietwert / Mietzinseinnahmen enter the Eigenmietwert from your assessment, or the rent you received if the property is let.

steps.title: Choose the deduction
steps.body: For Unterhalts- und Verwaltungskosten choose Pauschalabzug, which is 20% and needs no receipts. Choose the actual costs only if they were higher, and keep the invoices.

steps.title: Enter the tax value
steps.body: In the field Steuerwert enter the value from the assessment. The program carries the totals to line 6 (net income from property) and line 31.1 (property) of the main form.

steps.title: Declare your debts, then ask for the split
steps.body: Enter all your debts and the interest you paid in the Schuldenverzeichnis, not only the Swiss mortgage. Then paste the German note into the remarks: it asks the office to allocate the debt in proportion to where your assets lie, and shows the quota you calculated.

steps.title: Declare what you have elsewhere, for the rate
steps.body: Income and wealth abroad belong in the return even though Switzerland does not tax them. Leaving them out does not lower your bill, it simply invites the office to estimate them.

steps.title: Name a representative, then submit
steps.body: Give the office an address in Switzerland where post reaches you, because a decision can otherwise be served by publication in the official gazette (Art. 116 Abs. 2 DBG). The deadline is 31 March and can be extended online, free of charge, until 30 November.

glossary.beschraenkt: Limited tax liability. You are taxed here on the property alone, not on everything you own.
glossary.liegenschaftenverzeichnis: List of real estate. The form where every property is declared.
glossary.amtlicheSchaetzung: The cantonal valuation. It sets both figures the return asks for and arrives as a Schätzungsanzeige.
glossary.eigenmietwert: Notional rent. What the canton assumes a property brings in when you do not rent it out.
glossary.steuerwert: Tax value. The value the canton puts on the property for the wealth tax.
glossary.pauschalabzug: Flat deduction. 20% of the gross for maintenance and administration, with no receipts.
glossary.schuldzinsen: Debt interest. Deductible here only in the proportion your Swiss assets bear to everything you own.
glossary.satzbestimmend: Rate determining. Counted when the rate is chosen, but not taxed.
glossary.steuerausscheidung: Allocation. Dividing income and wealth between Switzerland and the country you live in.
glossary.vertretung: Representative. Somebody with a Swiss address who receives your tax post. Without one, a decision can be served by publication in the official gazette.
glossary.gemeindesteueramt: The municipal tax office where the property lies. Your first contact for anything unclear.
glossary.fristerstreckung: Extension of the filing deadline. Free of charge in Zurich, online, until 30 November.
glossary.bemerkungen: Remarks. The free text field where the German note goes.
glossary.selbstanzeige: Voluntary disclosure. Declaring a property you left out before, once, without a penalty.
